definition: Propositional knowledge is knowledge represented as statements or beliefs about how events are related, such as whether a cue truly predicts an outcome. In learning tasks, it can be retrieved very quickly and automatically, but with more time people can weigh other available information and revise their judgment.

reasons: The definition’s claim that propositional knowledge is “knowledge represented as statements or beliefs about how events are related” is not explicitly supported in the provided packet; the packet discusses a “propositional model” and “propositions” but does not define propositional knowledge in those terms.

The packet supports an interpretation involving “very fast and uncontrollable retrieval” of propositional knowledge and that, with more time, participants can consider other information; however, the definition’s broader framing (“In learning tasks, it can be retrieved… automatically, but with more time people can weigh other available information and revise their judgment”) includes general statements about retrieval and revision that are only partially evidenced by the specific contingency-learning discussion in the packet.
